pillars.principle: AI drafts, proposes, and accelerates — but a named human always owns, signs, and is accountable for the final number.
controls: Every AI-assisted output routes to a mandatory human reviewer with sign-off before it leaves the boundary (NAV, reconciliation, investor statement, regulatory filing); no auto-release for anything client- or regulator-facing.
Accountability register maps each AI use-case to a named owner (RACI), so there is always an identifiable person answerable to the board, auditors, and regulators — never 'the model decided'.
Materiality-tiered review: higher-risk / higher-value outputs require senior or four-eyes approval; the AI presents its work and confidence, the human adjudicates.
Reviewer attestation is captured in the audit trail (who approved, when, what they saw, what they changed) and reviewers are trained to spot over-reliance / automation bias.
pillars.reassurance: 'If AI produces a wrong NAV, who is on the hook?' — Answer: a named human signs every number; the AI is a tool, accountability never transfers to the machine.

pillars.principle: Client data stays where the law and the contract require it; the AI comes to the data, the data does not leak to the model.
controls: Jurisdiction-aware data routing and regional model deployments (in-region / EU / dedicated tenancy) with a data-residency map per fund and per jurisdiction, enforced by policy-as-code, not manual discretion.

Zero data retention / no-training contractual terms with model providers; enterprise deployment with encryption in transit and at rest, and tenant isolation so one client's data can never surface in another's session.

Data classification and DLP at the boundary: PII, MNPI, and cross-border transfers are tagged, minimized, and blocked from prompts unless the use-case is sanctioned; GDPR Art. 44-49 transfer basis documented.
Regional key management and the ability to prove — per record — where it was processed and under which legal basis, for regulator and client due-diligence questionnaires.
pillars.reassurance: 'Will our data leave the jurisdiction, get co-mingled, or train someone else's model?' — Answer: contractual zero-retention, in-region processing, tenant isolation, and a provable residency map.

pillars.pillar: Source Citation, Explainability & Full Audit Trail
pillars.principle: No unsourced numbers — every AI output is traceable to its inputs, its prompt, its model version, and the human who approved it.
controls: Retrieval-grounded outputs with inline citations back to source documents (trust deeds, trade files, GL, custodian feeds); ungrounded / uncited claims are flagged and cannot be used as the basis for a booked figure.
Immutable, tamper-evident logging of prompt, retrieved context, model + version, output, confidence, reviewer, and edits — retained per records-retention schedule and exportable for audit.
Full reproducibility: any historical output can be reconstructed with the exact model version, data snapshot, and configuration in force at the time (versioned, pinned models — no silent upgrades).
Lineage view that lets an auditor trace a final number backward through the AI step to the underlying evidence in a few clicks.
pillars.reassurance: 'When the auditor or regulator asks how this figure was derived, can we show our work?' — Answer: end-to-end citation and an immutable, reproducible trail from source to signature.

pillars.principle: AI operates strictly within each user's existing entitlements and never becomes a back door around SoD.
controls: The AI inherits the requesting user's RBAC/entitlements — it can only see and act on data that user is already authorized for; no privilege elevation via the assistant.
SoD enforced across the AI workflow: the identity that prepares/AI-drafts cannot also approve; maker-checker preserved and the AI cannot occupy both roles.
Least-privilege, per-use-case service accounts for AI system access, with secrets management, session logging, and periodic access recertification.
Prompt-injection and tool-permission guardrails so the model cannot be coerced into actions or data access outside its sanctioned scope.
pillars.reassurance: 'Could someone use the AI to see data they shouldn't, or to both prepare and approve?' — Answer: AI runs inside existing entitlements and SoD; it can't elevate privilege or collapse maker-checker.

pillars.principle: AI models are governed like any other model of consequence — inventoried, independently validated, monitored, and re-approved on a lifecycle.
controls: Central model inventory with risk-tiering (aligned to SR 11-7-style MRM and EU AI Act tiers); each use-case has a documented risk assessment, intended use, and limitations.

Independent validation before go-live and periodic revalidation: benchmark test sets, accuracy/precision thresholds, bias and drift testing, and defined acceptance criteria owned outside the build team.
Ongoing performance monitoring with drift/degradation alerts, KPIs, and automatic fallback to human-only processing when the model breaches thresholds.
Change control and a model-risk committee gate for new use-cases, model upgrades, and prompt/config changes; kill-switch and rollback procedures documented.
pillars.reassurance: 'How do you know the model is fit for purpose and stays that way?' — Answer: independent validation, tiered MRM governance, continuous monitoring, and a kill-switch — the same rigor as any material model.

pillars.principle: The system is designed to fail safe — it says 'I don't know', escalates uncertainty, and never fabricates a number to look complete.
controls: Retrieval-grounding + constrained outputs so the model answers from provided evidence, not memory; abstention and 'insufficient evidence' responses are first-class, not penalized.

Confidence scoring and mandatory human escalation on low-confidence, out-of-distribution, or high-materiality items; deterministic calculations (NAV math, tie-outs) done by validated engines, with AI used for reasoning/summarization, not arithmetic of record.
Automated validation harnesses: cross-footing, tolerance checks, reconciliation against golden sources, and adversarial/red-team test suites run before and during deployment.
Continuous error-rate tracking, incident logging, and feedback loops that feed corrections back into prompts, retrieval, and test sets.
pillars.reassurance: 'What if it just makes something up?' — Answer: grounded answers, enforced abstention, deterministic engines for the actual numbers, and tolerance checks that catch fabrication before a human ever sees it.

pillars.principle: One governed, transparent AI estate mapped to the control frameworks regulators already trust — replacing ungoverned shadow-AI with a safe, sanctioned path.
controls: Framework mapping and evidence: EU AI Act risk-tiering per use-case, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001/42001 for the platform, GDPR DPIAs, and SOX-style ITGC / control testing over AI-touched financial processes.
Sanctioned-AI provision: an approved, monitored enterprise tool that is genuinely better and easier than consumer chatbots, so staff have no reason to paste client data into unmanaged services.
Shadow-AI detection and policy enforcement (network/DLP controls blocking unsanctioned AI endpoints) plus a clear intake process to onboard new use-cases safely rather than driving them underground.
AI governance committee, written policy, mandatory training, vendor due-diligence, and periodic independent audit/attestation to keep alignment current as regulations evolve.
pillars.reassurance: 'How do we satisfy regulators across the group and stop staff quietly using ChatGPT with client data?' — Answer: use-cases mapped to EU AI Act / SOC 2 / ISO / GDPR / SOX evidence, plus a sanctioned tool good enough that shadow-AI disappears.
